items.note: The lemma (three stages give (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) and restore every scratch wire) and every paragraph of its proof are reproduced: the net change (JV+RG)x does not depend on a,c, the bit and complex central coefficients are given, and the three-stage composition is shown. But the copy, gather, scatter and side-injection maps and the neighbour rules they rely on (690-703) are never defined, so the coefficient claims rest on undefined maps. The wire counts W_b, W_c (767-782) are also absent.

Gives D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, with D_vD_u^{-1} applied on each edge. The proof follows the paper's invariant: stored array = D_v(logical) holds at the sources, and R-linearity makes a common frame commute with a pointwise gate. It then gives the signed route operator eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1}.

Several pieces match the paper: the form x^T(I-J/9)y and its triple inner products, the stage transitions and terminal labels, the side-wire inclusion via t_X perp t_Y, and the central-wire loss of P(x)F. So do the telescoping to Wm-2N, L=Ich, the total Wm-2N+2L, and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539. Missing are the gate-label table (eq:motif-labels, 975-988) and the per-edge residual check (1021-1064): the claim that only the central edge 3->4 decreases rests on quoting the paper's conclusion. The binary orthonormal-basis part of the lemma (1073-1102) is also absent.

Uses projections P_U at gates and sinks and -P_{U_a} at the X_a sources, with frames Phi_M. The steps are: rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V - dim U; the N exceptional source edges 2P_{U_a}, each of rank one; s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b with deficit N-2L_b>0; and the endpoint difference P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m. This is the paper's proof step for step.

States the phase frames C_U, one kernel aI+bX_v (or its inverse) per orthonormal residual vector, s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c<W_c m, and C^{(x)m} on every role after the corrections. The derivation has weight additivity mod 4 for orthogonal vectors, odd weight giving the kernel, and the X_a->Y_a pair with C^{-1} on 27 coordinates fixed by Z_{a,k} and i^{27k}. The k-column tensoring and the explicit q_V-q_U formula are only implicit.

Has L/N<1/2, s_b<W_b m and s_c<W_c m, the exact eta_b and eta_c, both above 20*2^{-50}, and log m<20. From these, m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-eta) gives s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, exactly as at 1331-1343.

The controlled-shift lemma is derived as in the paper's proof: split at Q-a and merge, b^{O(1)} offset work absorbed by Q, unit multiplication by c increasing pieces, negation by stack reversal. The elementary stream operations lemma is only stated by quotation (S0.1.1); its proof (513-550) is not reconstructed.

Follows both proofs. The factorization A=E_1 Pi E_2 comes from pivoting on the rightmost entry of the topmost nonzero row with lower-triangular operations. The shear then uses the prime q avoiding denominators, triangular transforms in descending order at O(V), and the conjugation by E_1 and E_2. Each one of Pi becomes three updates with a single interchange, giving exactly a recursive calls.

Reproduces the whole proof. It covers the k=0 base case, the cyclic split into W role streams of volume V/W, Phi_{A_e} on each edge via the matrix-shear lemma, and frames commuting with bit gates. Then come the endpoint identity giving Phi_{I_m}, the merge, and the three updates turning the shear into an interchange. It ends with s recursive calls, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) with its geometric sum, and the fixed-tape depth-first schedule including the one-bit-payload descriptor bound.

Follows the paper's proof. It takes k and rho=ceil(k log W/(2 log q)), peels high digits into a row field R=q^{2rho}>=W^k, pads to R'<2R, and splits e-rho in base m with the cost sum O(Ve^tau). Descriptor counts, binary padding to [q^e] and the unequal-width case are also given.

Conjugation by P_M with the residual basis as M's first columns is given. So are one forward child per slot, the inverse child via (C^{-1})^{(x)f}=(-i)^f Z C Z, row-addition decomposition of M, exactly s_c children on f=e/m axes, and H_0^{(x)D}=b^D S_D C^{(x)D} S_D. All of this matches the paper.

Reproduces the proof: the eight conditional updates and their parity cycles, the packed lines as cyclic shifts, and the bad set B with delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}}. T_0S_0^{-1} permutes B, rotations are conjugated by chunk swaps, and B is repaired by extraction and radix sort. The full time bound and its o(1) extra terms follow, and so does the use for row additions. The headline drops the family conditions, but S0.1.5.4.15 supplies them. One sub-step misphrases the guard argument; see the errors list.

Covers the node overhead O(V((eK)^tau+1)), the rows from the first q_0 chunks padded to a multiple of W^{k_0}, and the u=Wg+w split giving V/W children. Then come F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1) with leaves O(e) at e<d^beta, K<=e^{c/beta}, the internal and leaf sums, and the base-m pieces giving O(d^{lambda'}) for max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}<lambda'<1 (S0.1.5.6.7). The headline S0.1.5.6 loosens the lambda' condition.

Gives the O(Vd^{lambda'}) layer with one final truncation and error < sqrt2 2^{-p}. It also has the guard-width calculation: E, B, nu, C_1, C_0, Delta, depth recurrence A(e)<=sA(e/m)+E, the depth-to-size induction, and Delta=o(p) from epsilon C_1<1. The proof's uniform packed-call bound and the conversion back to H are included.

Covers character cancellation by the sign-changing shift, the DIF step, and bit-reversed storage B_t with the opposite procedure F^+B^{-1}. The layout L (prefix moves O(TpdK), Dq-1 chunk exchanges O(Tp pK^{tau-1})), the simultaneous layer per round, monomial twiddles, single truncation per round, error sqrt2 ell 2^{-p}, and LBF^- / F^+B^{-1}L^{-1} are all present, following 2819-3200.

The steps are: evaluation at B_0=2^{4p}, the separation |h_j|<=r2^{2p}<B_0/2, two's-complement packing with carry in {-1,0}, and centred extraction with carry in {0,1}. These are followed by the real/imaginary streams, the negacyclic wrap, |H_j|<=r2^{2p}, truncation by p+ell bits, and four products dominating the cost, as in the proof.

Includes the normalisation identity via F^-(f*g)=M F^-f F^-g and F^+F^-=I/M, and P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v). The error chain 2delta, +eta, 3delta+eta, times M = sqrt2 M(3ell+1)2^{-p} and the cost O(Tp log(rp)) for the M=T/r products also follow the paper's proof.

Uses N=CTD, the cited Gaussian identity and ||N-I|| bound, Neumann invertibility, and the normalisations S', J', D' with product 2^{-2alpha^2}. The left inverse gives P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA. Ordered numerical maps with errors and costs, the in-order selection C and the Neumann sum cost are included, as are the tensor form, linewise costs, axis exposure O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau)) and per-line setup.

The chirp's period and the coefficient check give QF_t = conj(a)(a*(conj(a)u))/T. The dilation identity F^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F^+ gives RF^+R=F^+, R commutes with the pointwise product, and the convolution rule gives (u*v)/S^2. The conjugation trick for RF^+ is included. All as in the paper.

Lists the fixed exponents, the sizes b, p, d, K, T, r and t_i, and the comparison constants. It sets alpha, gamma and eta, uses the Rosser-Schoenfeld/HvdH prime count and disjoint intervals, and derives T/2<S<T by Bernoulli and alpha^4 theta_i>p. The trial-division search in n^{o(1)}, no wraparound, and c_j<2^{3b} complete it, all following 4016-4193.

Shows Phi is an isomorphism because the image of x has order S. The triangular digit formula is given, with updates in order i=d..1. On the padded box each step is a bijection that keeps the zero padding. Each update is a prefix-controlled cyclic shift, and axis reversal by O(d^2) moves gives O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau)). This is the paper's argument.

The exact identity is derived as in 4303-4342: the map is well defined, diagonal and invertible, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h=zeta^j holds, and M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T. The computed twist procedure (the steps f', g', h' and the untwist, with approximate phases of error <2*2^{-p}, 4374-4402) is not described. Only its error contributions appear later, in S0.4.6.9.4.

Covers chirp construction, the computed chirp transform x_0, y_0, C(x), the source transform 2^gamma B_0 QF_t A = RF_s, and its conjugate F^+. Digit extraction at 2^{-b-2} and the six steps follow, with the two S scales undoing (u*v)/S^2. The headline S0.4.6 misnames the second scale; S0.4.6.7 has it right (see errors).

Follows the error chain: E_ring<5TL, the disk margin .701, M_C<6TL, chirp <8TL, E_s=9*2^gamma TL, and z within (2E_s+2). Then (3E_s+2), E_w=S(3E_s+2)<28*2^gamma T^2L, ||w||<1/16, and the final 448b2^{-b+gamma}<=448b2^{-3b/4}<1/2. Unique rounding, the capacity bound, and carry propagation with bounded carries to 2n bits complete it.

V=Tp=Theta(n) and the seven normalized rows are justified from their lemmas. The margins g_1..g_7 give min = 2^{-181} = 2kappa. Setup p^{A+C}=o(Tp) and exceptional sorting o(V) follow, log p powers are absorbed into p^kappa, and the total is O(n(log n)^{1-kappa}), with schoolbook multiplication below a cutoff. This is the paper's accounting.

S0 only says the bound refutes the n log n optimality conjecture in this model. It never states what an eventual lower bound requires, the liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n)=0 negation, or that the power saving gives limit zero along all lengths.

errors.says: The method uses the one-bit identity 'H_0 = beta S C S' coordinatewise.
errors.paper: The identity is H_0 = b S C S with b=(1-i)/2 (eq:phase-basic-identities, 1827); the layer identity has scalar b^D (1930). In the paper beta denotes the recursion threshold 1/2 (2394), so writing beta for the scalar confuses two quantities. The headline of S0.1.5.3 itself gives the correct scalar ((1-i)/2)^D.

errors.says: Each coordinate moves by at most four, 'so with ten guard values on either side no segment leaves its quotient range'.
errors.paper: The paper says the displacement is at most four 'even if an intermediate point leaves its starting quotient square' (2049-2052). The guard condition 10<=g<=2^{K-1}-11 is used differently: it puts each K-bit segment in [20,2^K-21], so a displacement of eight keeps it inside [0,2^K-1] and there is no carry or borrow between segments (2085-2091). It does not keep a segment inside its quotient range.

errors.says: The recurrence 'sums to O(d^{lambda'}) over the base-m pieces for any fixed lambda'<1'.
errors.paper: The bound O(d^{lambda'}) is claimed only for fixed lambda' with max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}<lambda'<1 (2442-2444). Sub-step S0.1.5.6.7 states this correctly.

errors.says: The algorithm ends with 'rescaling by S and 2^{2b+4}, rounding, ...'.
errors.paper: The second scale is by 2^{2b+4}S, so S enters twice and undoes two different normalisations (4521-4523, 4536-4540). Sub-steps S0.4.6.7 and S0.4.6.8 state this correctly.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound. It builds the scalar bank-exchange network, then frames, labels and the dimension budget, then the bit shear interface (s_b<W_b m) and the exponent tau=1-2^{-50}. Matrix shears and the recurrence give O(Ve^tau) interchange, which extends to all widths. The complex phase interface, packed row additions and the layer recurrence give O(Vd^{lambda'}). Synthetic transforms, convolution, resampling with chirp and permutation cancellation, CRT, the twist, exact recovery and the cost table finish the argument. Almost every link is carried by a quoted paper sentence, so the chain does not break. It is thinnest in three places: the gate definitions behind the scalar network's coefficients, the explicit gate-label and residual tables behind 'only central 3->4 edges decrease', and the computed twist procedure, all of which are cited rather than reconstructed.

steps.note: The fixed linear network exchanging the banks, (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a) in three stages, and restoring every scratch wire is stated and derived. Triples of [100] are present. N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are never defined numerically: N is used without definition and m appears only as dim F^{(x)3}.

A common invertible frame per gate commutes with a pointwise gate, so the network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}. Each edge applies only D_vD_u^{-1}, and the intermediate frames are free to be chosen cheaply.
Labels are nondegenerate subspaces of the m-dimensional F^{(x)3}, nested on every edge. The only decreasing edges are the central wires from time 3 to 4, each losing h (S0.1.3.4.1).
rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U for nested nondegenerate labels, unchanged by reversing the edge. The N source edges 2P_{U_a} are the rank-one exceptions.
Sum of |Delta dim| = Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich (telescoping at gates, Ic decreasing edges of loss h), and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.
L_b/N=100/539 and L_c/N=101/539, both below 1/2, give the deficit N-2L_b>0 and hence s<Wm.
On X_a the endpoint difference is P_{U_a^perp}+P_{U_a}=I_m; every other role has zero source matrix and identity sink matrix. Hence Phi_{I_m}, i.e. H<-H+D, on every role, scratch rows included.
A=E_1 Pi E_2 with a ones; the shear costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V), each one a recursive call. Summed over edges, a node makes exactly s calls.
Children have volume V/W, so F_0=O(1) and F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1). With eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20, s/W<m^tau for tau=1-2^{-50}, and the geometric sum gives F_k=O(e^tau).

central.summary: All nine steps of the central saving are reconstructed with their defining content and in their place in the chain. The plan builds the bank-exchange network, frames, nested labels, rank = dimension change with the N rank-one source exceptions, the budget Wm-2N+2L and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b, and L/N<1/2. It then gives the endpoint shear, edges as exactly s recursive interchanges, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. The only thinness is that N and m=h^3 are not defined numerically, and the gate-label table behind C3 is quoted as a conclusion rather than built.
